catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 3 maintenance supplemental topline results
detailed_catalyst_text: Topline results from the supplemental Part 2 of the Phase 3 ulcerative colitis maintenance program were reported, expanding efficacy and safety data in a highly refractory population. Continued 50 mg therapy produced clinically meaningful remission in induction non-responders, dose escalation recaptured remission in relapsers, and exposure-adjusted malignancy rates were consistent with expected ulcerative colitis background rates, strengthening the long-term safety database.
catalyst_text_evidence: PARIS, France – 2026-06-29 – 10:05 pm CEST – Abivax SA (PARIS:FR, NASDAQ:ABVX) ("Abivax" or the "Company"), a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing therapeutics that harness the body’s natural regulatory mechanisms to stabilize the immune response in patients with chronic inflammatory diseases, today announced topline results from ABTECT Maintenance Part 2, the supplemental portion of its Phase 3 UC maintenance program evaluating obefazimod, its investigational oral miR-124 enhancer, in adults with moderately to severely active UC. Obefazimod delivered meaningful clinical benefit in a highly refractory ulcerative colitis ("UC") population, with 37.2% of induction non-responders achieving clinical remission and 34.5% achieving endoscopic remission at Week 44 following continued 50 mg treatment. Dose escalation to obefazimod 50 mg recaptured clinical remission in 45.5% of patients who relapsed during ABTECT Maintenance Part 1, supporting a practical dose-escalation strategy for regaining and sustaining disease control over time. Across the integrated Phase 2 and Phase 3 UC program (1,704 patient-years of exposure), exposure-adjusted incidence rates ("EAIRs") for malignancies excluding non-melanoma skin cancer ("NMSC") were 0.35 and 0.64 events per 100 patient-years ("PYs"), and for NMSC were 0.59 and 0.64 events per 100 PYs in the all-active combined (50 mg + 25 mg) and 50 mg cohorts respectively, all consistent with expected UC background rates. In ABTECT Maintenance Part 2, EAIRs for malignancies excluding NMSC were 0.48 and 0.69 events per 100 PYs, and for NMSC were 0.95 and 0.69 events per 100 PYs, in the all-active combined and 50 mg cohorts respectively, all consistent with expected UC background rates.

catalyst_text: Announced positive topline Phase 3 maintenance results
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive topline data from the 44-week Phase 3 ABTECT maintenance trial in adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis showed both 25 mg and 50 mg doses met the primary endpoint of clinical remission and all key secondary endpoints. Clinical remission occurred in about 51% on treatment versus 10% on placebo, and safety was favorable with no new signals. These results support the potential of a once-daily oral maintenance therapy.

The results demonstrate that both the 25 mg and 50 mg doses of obefazimod met the primary endpoint of clinical remission and all key secondary endpoints at Week 44. Obefazimod demonstrated a favorable safety profile over the 44-week maintenance trial (N=580), with no new safety signals.

catalyst_text: Presented rapid symptomatic improvements and favorable safety profile
detailed_catalyst_text: New clinical analyses from the Phase 3 ABTECT-1 and ABTECT-2 induction trials in moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis were presented, showing early symptomatic response by week 1 and symptomatic remission by week 2 with safety comparable to placebo. A pooled safety analysis reported similar rates of serious TEAEs and discontinuations versus placebo, and biomarker data showed miR-124 upregulation with reductions in IL-17A and IL-6. These findings support rapid efficacy onset, tolerability, and the proposed mechanism of action in ulcerative colitis.

catalyst_text: Reported positive preclinical anti fibrotic activity in models
detailed_catalyst_text: New preclinical data presented showed anti-fibrotic activity in inflammatory bowel disease models, with significant reductions in fibrosis biomarkers and fibroblast activation markers. Dual anti-inflammatory and anti-fibrotic effects were observed in both an in vitro human fibroblast system and an in vivo animal model. These results suggest potential to address fibrosis, a key unmet need particularly relevant to Crohn’s disease.
